Definition: to open (the senses, especially the eyes); figuratively, to be observant
BiblicalUsage: Pâqach is to open, especially the eyes and the senses. The serpent promises their eyes shall be opened, and the eyes of them both are opened and they know they are naked; Elisha prays, LORD, open his eyes, and the young man sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire; and Isaiah promises the eyes of the blind shall be opened.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe opened eyes are the story of the whole Bible. The serpent opens eyes to shame, the LORD opens eyes to see His armies, and one day He opens the blind eyes for good.
